reply.english: Yes, the building has a lift.
From the first of the month.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: And peace be upon you.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: عندي شقّة حلوة قريبة من المسجد
dialogue.english: I have a nice flat near the masjid.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: The flat suits me very well.

pair.english: How much is the monthly rent?
How many bedrooms does it have?

response.english: Yes, the building has a lift.
From the first of the month.

lessons.culture: In Saudi Arabia rent is often quoted by the year rather than by the month, so ask which one the price is. Always ask whether water and electricity are included, and sign a written lease before you pay anything. The owner of the building is called صاحب العمارة, and the price is in riyals.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I am looking for a flat to rent."

too_formal.feedback: أبحث عن is written Arabic. In Hejazi, looking for something is أدوّر على.

exercises.tip: أدوّر على (adawwir 3ala) is "I look for". Simply saying أبغى شقة للإيجار, "I want a flat to rent", also works.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I want a one-year lease."

too_formal.feedback: أريد is written Arabic. Hejazi says أبغى.

exercises.tip: Hejazi أبغى (abgha) is "I want", never أبي.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Is there a lift?"
exercises.tip: Some people say أسانسير (asanseer) for a lift.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence asks about the monthly rent?
exercises.tip: بكم (bikam) asks "how much is ...".

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: "للإيجار / شقّة / على / أدوّر" (I am looking for a flat to rent.)
Put the words in order: "التاني / الدور / في / هي" (It is on the second floor.)
Complete: "كم _____ نوم فيها؟" (How many bedrooms does it have?)
exercises.tip: أوضة (ooDa) is a room in Hejazi; the plural is أوض.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "تفضّل، دي _____ الشقّة" (Here are the keys to the flat.)
exercises.tip: مفتاح (miftaa7) is a key; the plural is مفاتيح.

exercises.prompt: You hear: "بكم الإيجار في الشهر؟" Say: two thousand riyals a month.
exercises.tip: ألفين (alfeen) is "two thousand".

exercises.prompt: You hear: "فيه مصعد؟" Say: yes, the building has a lift.

too_formal.feedback: نعم and المبنى are written Arabic. Hejazi says إيوه and العمارة.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: Please come in.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: مَا شَاءَ اللهُ، واسعة مرّة. الشقّة مفروشة؟
dialogue.transliteration: maa shaa2a Allaah, waas3a marra. ish-shigga mafroosha?
dialogue.english: Mashallah, it is very spacious. Is the flat furnished?

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: ولا يهمّك، صلّحه وأنا حاخد الشقّة
dialogue.transliteration: wala yihimmak, Salli7u wa ana 7aakhud ish-shigga
dialogue.english: No problem, fix it and I will take the flat.

pair.english: How many bathrooms are in the flat?
Where do I put the fridge?

lessons.culture: A flat is described by its rooms: the living room (الصالة, or المجلس where guests are received), the bedrooms, the kitchen and the bathrooms. A flat may be rented furnished or empty, so ask exactly what stays, such as the fridge, the wardrobes and the air conditioners.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Where is the kitchen?"

too_formal.feedback: أين is written Arabic. Hejazi asks with فين.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Is the flat furnished?"

too_formal.feedback: هل is not used in speech. Hejazi just raises the voice: الشقّة مفروشة؟

exercises.tip: عفش (3afsh) is the everyday word for furniture.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "There is a sofa in the living room"?
exercises.tip: Some people say المجلس (il-majlis) for the living room.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence asks how many bathrooms are in the flat?
exercises.tip: After كم (kam) the counted noun is singular: كم حمّام.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: "هنا / الطاولة / حُطّ" (Put the table here.)
exercises.tip: To a woman: حُطّي الطاولة هنا.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: "مرّة / واسعة / النوم / أوضة" (The bedroom is very spacious.)
exercises.tip: مرّة (marra) is "very" in Hejazi.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "فين _____؟" (Where is the wardrobe?)
exercises.tip: Some people also say الخزانة (il-khizaana).

exercises.prompt: Complete: "_____ شغّال؟" (Does the air conditioner work?)
exercises.tip: شغّال (shaghghaal) means "working".

exercises.prompt: You hear: "فين المطبخ؟" Say: next to the living room.

too_formal.feedback: بجانب and غرفة الجلوس are written Arabic. Hejazi says جنب and الصالة.

exercises.prompt: You hear: "كم حمّام في الشقّة؟" Say: two bathrooms.
exercises.tip: The -een ending (حمّامين) means "two".

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you, Yusuf.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: And peace be upon you.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: تمام. والباب كمان ما يتسكّر كويّس
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam. wil-baab kamaan ma yitsakkar kwayyis
dialogue.english: Fine. And the door does not close well either.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: حاشوفه بعد شوية. الكهربا مقطوعة في البيت؟
dialogue.english: I will look at it in a little while. Is the power out in the house?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: No, but the light bulb does not work.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: May Allah reward you with good.

lessons.culture: A home repair is often a favour between brothers, relatives or neighbours before anyone is paid, and the helper is thanked with جَزَاكَ اللهُ خَيْرًا. People say الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ when a job ends well. A professional such as a plumber (سبّاك) or an electrician (كهربائي) is called when the problem is beyond a simple fix, and it is polite to ask the cost before the work starts.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "The tap is leaking water."

too_formal.feedback: صنبور, يسرّب and ماء are written Arabic. Hejazi says الحنفية, تنزّ and موية.

exercises.tip: نزّ (nazz) is "to leak" or "to drip".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Where is the toolbox?"

too_formal.feedback: أين is written Arabic. Hejazi asks with فين.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Pass me the screwdriver"?
exercises.tip: ناولني (naawilni) is "pass me".

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "The power is out in the house"?
exercises.tip: الكهربا (il-kahraba) is the everyday short form of الكهرباء.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: "ومسامير / شاكوش / أبغى" (I need a hammer and nails.)
Put the words in order: "كويّس / يتسكّر / ما / الباب" (The door does not close well.)
Complete: "الباب ما _____ كويّس" (The door does not close well.)
exercises.tip: سكّر (sakkar) is "to close"; يتسكّر is "it gets closed".

exercises.prompt: Complete: "اتصل بالـ_____ لو احتجت" (Call the plumber if needed.)
exercises.tip: كهربائي (kahrabaa2i) is an electrician.

exercises.prompt: You hear: "تقدر تصلّحه؟" Say: yes, I will try.

too_formal.feedback: نعم and سأحاول are written Arabic. Hejazi says إيوه and حاحاول.

exercises.tip: حـ (7a-) before a verb makes it future: حاحاول, "I will try".

exercises.prompt: You hear: "شكراً، اشتغل دحين." Reply.
exercises.tip: This is fixed Islamic wording, said the same way in every dialect.

phrases.arabic: إحنا ساكنين في الشقّة اللي جنبكم

reply.english: May Allah reward you with good.
In the bin at the entrance.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: And peace be upon you.

pair.english: Which flat do you live in?
Where do we put the rubbish?

response.english: In the bin at the entrance.
May Allah reward you with good.

lessons.culture: Islam gives the neighbour a great right, so neighbours share food, visit one another when ill, look after each other's homes and avoid disturbing each other with noise. Sending a dish to the new family next door is a common way to start a friendship, and the answer is جَزَاكَ اللهُ خَيْرًا. Offering tea is the usual first step towards a visit.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "We are your new neighbours."

too_formal.feedback: نحن is written Arabic. Hejazi says إحنا.

exercises.tip: إحنا (i7na) is "we" in Hejazi.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Where do we put the rubbish?"

too_formal.feedback: أين, نضع and النفايات are written Arabic. Hejazi says فين, نحط and الزبالة.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "I brought you some food"?
exercises.tip: جاب (jaab) is "to bring" in Hejazi.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "A neighbour has a right over us"?
options: إحنا ساكنين في الشقّة اللي جنبكم

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: "شقّة / أي / في / ساكن / إنت" (Which flat do you live in?)
exercises.tip: To a woman: إنتِ ساكنة في أي شقّة؟

exercises.prompt: Put the pieces in order: "لو سمحت؟ / سيارتك / تحرّك / ممكن" (Could you move your car, please?)
Complete: "ممكن أستلف _____؟" (May I borrow a ladder?)
exercises.tip: أستلف (astalif) is "I borrow".

exercises.prompt: Complete: "جبت لكم شوية _____" (I brought you some food.)
You hear: "جبت لكم شوية أكل." Reply.
exercises.tip: This is fixed Islamic wording, said the same way in every dialect. To a woman: جَزَاكِ اللهُ خَيْرًا.

exercises.prompt: You hear: "تعال اشرب شاهي معانا." Say: God willing, another time.
accepted: إن شاء الله، في وقت ثاني
إن شاء الله في وقت ثاني

too_formal.item: إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ، فِي وَقْتٍ آخَر
too_formal.feedback: آخر is written Arabic. Hejazi says وقت ثاني.

exercises.tip: شاهي (shaahi) is "tea" in Hejazi.

challenge.title: Viewing a Flat
challenge.instructions: Write and act out a conversation of at least 10 lines in which you ask about a flat for rent, its bedrooms, floor and monthly rent, ask to see it, ask whether it is furnished, find the kitchen, and say that you will take it. Use at least 8 target phrases from Unit 18, and use فين, بكم and دحين the Hejazi way.
required_elements: A greeting, السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ, and its reply.
A question about the rent or the number of bedrooms, using بكم or كم.
A question about the floor, the lift, or whether water and electricity are included.
A request to see the flat, using أقدر أشوف.
A question about the kitchen or the furniture, using فين or مفروشة.
A closing decision with حاخدها or أبغى عقد إيجار, and جَزَاكَ اللهُ خَيْرًا with its reply وَإِيَّاكَ.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ، أدوّر على شقّة للإيجار. بكم الإيجار في الشهر؟
dialogue.transliteration: as-salaamu 3alaykum, adawwir 3ala shigga lil-eejaar. bikam il-eejaar fish-shahr?
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you. I am looking for a flat to rent. How much is the monthly rent?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ. ألفين ريال في الشهر، وفيها تلات أوض نوم
dialogue.transliteration: wa 3alaykumu as-salaam. alfeen riyaal fish-shahr, wa feeha talaat uwaD noom
dialogue.english: And peace be upon you. Two thousand riyals a month, and it has three bedrooms.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.transliteration: fi ayy door? wa feeh maS3ad?
dialogue.english: Which floor? And is there a lift?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: في الدور التاني، والعمارة فيها مصعد
dialogue.english: On the second floor, and the building has a lift.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.transliteration: agdar ashoof ish-shigga? wa hiya mafroosha?
dialogue.english: Can I view the flat? And is it furnished?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: تفضّل. فيها عفش كامل، والمطبخ جنب الصالة
dialogue.transliteration: tfaDDal. feeha 3afsh kaamil, wil-maTbakh jamb iS-Saala
dialogue.english: Please come in. It has full furniture, and the kitchen is next to the living room.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: الأوضة واسعة مرّة! الموية والكهربا داخلة في الإيجار؟
dialogue.transliteration: il-ooDa waas3a marra! il-mooya wil-kahraba daakhla fil-eejaar?
dialogue.english: The room is very spacious! Are water and electricity included in the rent?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: No, you pay for them.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.arabic: تمام، حاخدها. وأبغى عقد إيجار لسنة
dialogue.english: Fine, I will take it. And I want a one-year lease.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: Good. Please, here are the keys to the flat.

dialogue.speaker: Yusuf
dialogue.english: May Allah reward you with good.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.english: And you too.
